props.title: Scanners II: The New Order

sections.content: Scanners II: The New Order represents a fascinating shift in how Canadian horror cinema approached sequels in the early 90s. While David Cronenberg's original Scanners (1981) established the blueprint for telepathic horror with its legendary exploding head scene and corporate conspiracy themes, this Christian Duguay-directed follow-up takes the concept in a more action-oriented direction. The film follows David Kellum, a veterinary student who discovers his scanner abilities, getting pulled into a dark plot involving corrupt police officials and forced scanner drug addiction.

sections.content: What makes Scanners II particularly noteworthy is how it builds on the original's themes of institutional control while incorporating elements of police corruption narratives popular in the early 90s. The film's focus on drug dependency among scanners adds another layer of social commentary, though handled with less subtlety than Cronenberg's work. Director Christian Duguay, who would later helm Screamers (1995), brings a more conventional but still effective approach to the material.

The film fits into a larger trend of Canadian genre films from this era that includes The Vindicator (1986) and Pin (1988) - productions that attempted to balance commercial appeal with the body horror traditions established by Cronenberg. While the practical effects don't quite reach the heights of the original, sequences like the psychic duels and telekinetic violence maintain the franchise's visceral impact. sections.content: The early 90s marked a transition period for Canadian horror, as filmmakers moved away from the pure body horror of the 70s and 80s toward more commercially viable hybrids. Scanners II exemplifies this shift, maintaining elements of psychological horror while incorporating more conventional action sequences and conspiracy plots similar to films like They Live (1988).
